.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

In the superolateral aspect of the patella there is a T2 bright focus with irregular sclerotic margination seen on the plain film characterized by low signal margination on MRI. This focal lesion has central T2 bright signal similar in signal to articular cartilage and has a linear cartilaginous signal extending posteriorly to the articular surface of patella. The articular cartilage of patella directly posterior to this focus is intact but does demonstrate slight contour irregularity and signal change which may represent mild chondrosis. The finding measures about 1 cm in maximum diameter. The appearance is typical in location and MRI features of a dorsal defect of the patella. This represents a normal anatomic variant.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The TT-TG distance measures about 1.5 cm, at the upper limits of normal, consistent with an element of mild lateralization of the tibial tubercle

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

Within the lateral femoral condyle there is a serpiginously marginated lesion measuring 2.1 AP, 1.4 cm with an 0.9 cm in depth situated 2 to 3 mm deep to the cortex of the lateral femoral condyle. The rim of this lesion is T2 bright and T1 dark with central fat. MR features are typical of a bone infarct. No evidence of cortical collapse.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a trace Baker's cyst demonstrated. No significant knee effusion is demonstrated.

A few small subcentimeter popliteal lymph nodes are incidentally noted.

Marrow signal is otherwise normal. No other bone infarcts are seen within field-of-view.

INTERPRETATION: 
Subcortical chondroid focus in the superolateral aspect of patella has MR features typical of a dorsal defect of the patella. The finding is not typical of a chondroblastoma. Mild overlying chondromalacia patella.

Mild lateralization of tibial tubercle.

Trace Baker's cyst.

There is a bone infarct seen in the lateral femoral condyle. No evidence of articular collapse.
Clinical correlation as to the possible cause of a bone infarct in this patient is recommended.

Report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] male complaining of left knee pain and swelling. Ultrasound shows focal tear of the lateral collateral ligament versus ligament sprain and likely tear of the medial and lateral meniscus. Joint effusion in the suprapatellar recess and Baker's cyst. Recommended by radiologist.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is mild thickening and increased T2 signal in the proximal fibers of the patellar tendon. Findings are consistent with mild patellar tendinosis. Quadriceps and patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint demonstrates mild chondral fraying at the patellar apex and also within the femoral trochlea but overall cartilage is reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is mild non-surfacing signal seen in the posterior horn of medial meniscus peripherally. Involving posterior horn near the posterior root attachment of medial meniscus there is mild apical truncation and fraying of the meniscus consistent with a subtle radial tear. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment demonstrates regions of chondral fraying and thinning with a few subcortical cysts seen within the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle in keeping with moderate chondrosis.

There is a subtle tear in the lateral meniscus involving anterior horn and anterior body in keeping with the radial tear in this region. There is also a horizontal signal in keeping with a horizontal tear extending into the anterior horn of lateral meniscus. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment demonstrates chondral fraying and thinning but is reasonably well-maintained. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis. Minimal degenerative spurring to the lateral joint compartment is noted.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, the fibular collateral ligament, the biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst. There is edema and fluid seen around the pes anserine tendons consistent with pes anserine bursitis.

There is a small knee effusion. Mild reactive synovitis is noted.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Mild tricompartmental chondrosis with early degenerative spurring to the lateral joint margin.

Subtle meniscal tears to the lateral and medial menisci as described.

Small Baker's cyst.

Pes anserine bursitis.

INDICATION:    assess mpfl tear, osteochondral fragment   .

PRIOR IMAGING:    
.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The patella is laterally subluxed and there is diffuse edema seen along the course of the medial patellofemoral ligament consistent with a high-grade injury. This extends to the femoral attachment and also involves the attachment at the patella. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is intraosseous edema within the medial patella and contour flattening of the medial surface of the patella. There is associated edema in the lateral femoral condyle consistent associated with the osteochondral impaction along the lateral cortical surface in keeping with transient lateral dislocation of the patella associated with osteochondral impaction of the medial surface of the patella and lateral femoral condyle.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is trochlea dysplasia and lateralization of the tibial tubercle with the TT-TG distance measuring 2.1 cm. Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates focal fraying at the patellar apex. The trochlear surface is reasonably well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment appears to be well maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is mild intrinsic signal within the posterior cruciate ligament but intact fibers are present and the signal changes may in part be artifactual.

There is edema around the proximal and mid fibers of the medial collateral ligament consistent with low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small to moderate knee effusion. There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Torn medial patellofemoral ligament associated with bone contusions an osteochondral fracturing of the medial surface of patella and lateral femoral condyle associated with transient dislocation of the patellofemoral joint.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

Low-grade medial collateral ligament tear.

Nonspecific signal in the posterior cruciate ligament favored to be artifactual.

Additional findings as noted.

МР данни за ограничен костно-мозъчен едем в областта на медиалния кондил на фемура, както  и субхондрално, в медиалното тибиално плато. Наличие на субхондрално разположени дребни кисти в медиалния кондил на фемура и в пателата. Хрущялът на пателата е със запазена дебелина. МР данни за увреда на медиалния менискус. Report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Pain worse with bending greater than 10 degrees. Swelling for 6 months.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable apart from very subtle increased signal seen in the proximal patellar tendon laterally. There is associated focal edema seen within Hoffa's fat pad inferior to the lateral aspect of the lower pole of patella also involving the lateral edge of the patellar tendon. Findings are consistent with mild lateral patellar tendinosis. Edema in Hoffa's fat may be associated with extensor mechanism impingement.

There is focal signal change and irregularity of the articular cartilage of the medial facet of patella consistent with moderate chondrosis. The remainder of the articular cartilage of patella is well-maintained. The trochlear articular cartilage is also reasonably preserved.

The TT-TG distance measures about 1 cm, within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus appears intact with no surfacing tear demonstrated. Immediately adjacent to the posterior horn of medial meniscus tracking along the joint margin posteriorly from the posterior root attachment medially to the medial joint margin deep to the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons there is a large multiloculated parameniscal cyst. This measures about 3.7 cm in length with short axis measurements of up to 1.2 x 0.9 cm.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.

There is no Baker's cyst or knee effusion demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Mild patellar tendinosis with edema in Hoffa's fat pad laterally. The edema may indicate presence of extensor mechanism impingement of Hoffa's fat pad.

There is a large para meniscal cyst closely associated with the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus. There is no discernible, associated medial meniscal tear identified.

No evidence of internal derangement.

INDICATION:    [Age] [Gender] with right knee pain giving way for one year worse going up and down stairs. No history of injury. Physiotherapy feels instability. Please assess for ligament damage.

.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is mild thickening and increased T2 signal in the proximal fibers of the patellar tendon consistent with mild patellar tendinosis. There is also mild prepatellar edema consistent with prepatellar bursitis.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates severe chondral fraying with some regions of focal cartilage loss seen to the lateral facet and apex of the patella. These changes are associated with subcortical cyst formation and edema seen to the patella involving lateral facet and apex.
The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea is reasonably well-maintained apart from mild fissuring seen at the medial femoral trochlear articular surface.

The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained with only mild chondral fraying.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small ganglion cyst projecting posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 1.4 x 0.9 x 0.6 cm. Centrally within this ganglion cyst there is a small loose body measuring 6 mm.

No significant knee effusion is detected. No significant Baker's cyst.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe chondrosis and involving the patellofemoral joint.

Mild patellar tendinosis. Associated prepatellar bursitis.

Mild chondrosis to the medial joint compartment.

Small ganglion cyst behind the posterior cruciate ligament with small loose body.

Παθολογικό σήμα αναγνωρίζεται και στο οπίσθιο κέρας του έξω μηνίσκου, ενώ μηνισκικό τεμάχιο ελέγχεται παρεκτοπισμένο στη μεσοκονδύλια εντομή. - Ακέραιος ελέγχεται ο έσω πλάγιος σύνδεσμος ενώ ο έξω πλάγιος αναγνωρίζεται με παθολογικό σήμα και κυματοειδή μορφολογία. - Ο ιγνυοπερονικός σύνδεσμος δεν αναγνωρίζεται. - Παθολογικό σήμα αναγνωρίζεται αντίστοιχα με την κατάφυση του ιγνυακού τένοντα. - Παρατηρείται παθολογικό σήμα στην άπω μοίρα του έσω και έξω πλατέος μυός καθώς και στις γαστέρες του γαστροκνημίου. - Αναγνωρίζεται μεγάλη ενδαρθρική συλλογή υγρού ανομοιογενούς έντασης σήματος, ως επί αίμαρθρου. - Δεν παρατηρούνται άξια λόγου ευρήματα από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού μηχανισμού. - Οιδηματώδης απεικόνιση των μαλακών μορίων πέριξ του γόνατος. Συμπέρασμα: 1. Πλήρης ρήξη πρόσθιου και οπίσθιου χιστού συνδέσμου. 2. Οίδημα οστικού μυελού στο πλαίσιο οστικών θλάσεων (bone bruises). 3. Οριζόντια ρήξη σώματος και οπισθίου κέρατος έσω μηνίσκου και ρήξη έξω μηνίσκου δίκην "λαβής κάδου" (bucket handle). 4. Πλήρης ρήξη έξω πλαγίου συνδέσμου και ιγνυοπερονικού συνδέσμου και ρήξη κατάφυσης ιγνυακού τένοντα. 5. Διατατική κάκωση μυών πέριξ του γόνατος ως περιγράφονται. 6. Σημαντική ποσότητα αίμαρθρου.

5. R/O bone contusion in the anterior aspect of proximal tibia, the fibular head, and the lateral femoral condyle.
6. Subcutaneous edema over anteromedial and posteromedial aspect of left knee.

Suggest correlate with clinical manifestation and further management.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Focal osteochondral injury at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with adjacent confluent bone marrow edema. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst with internal calcific body. Multiple intra-articular bodies, including a 1.1 cm ossific body at the anterior joint recess and a 0.8 cm ossific body at the posterior joint recess. Post arthroscopy scarring of Hoffa's fat pad.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tear of the medial meniscus, with maceration and complete radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Posterior medial displacement of a meniscal flap in the region of the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with areas of high-grade fissuring at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea. Articular surface remodeling at the lateral patellar facet. High-grade articular cartilage loss at the medial trochlea and medial facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Scarring.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Fragmentation of the tibial tubercle, reflecting the chronic sequela of remote Osgood-Schlatter disease.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Small subchondral insufficiency fracture at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with associated confluent bone marrow edema. No significant articular surface depression.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartments, where it is severe. Small knee joint effusion with multiple ossific intra-articular bodies measuring up to 1.1 cm. Small leaking Baker's cyst.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with dominant radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Displacement of a meniscal flap to the posteromedial joint recess.

Report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Three-week history of left knee pain after slipping on a wet floor and slamming knee into wall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral aspect of the medial femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal spurring, most notably along the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate complex multilobulated Baker's cyst with calcified bodies and synovial proliferation.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex degenerative tearing involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess. Superimposed reactive marrow edema at the medial tibial margin.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse full-thickness cartilage loss about the weightbearing medial femoral condyle with scattered areas of subchondral marrow edema and cystic change. Additional diffuse cartilage loss along the anterior and central medial tibial plateau with scattered subchondral marrow edema.


LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degenerative signal posterior horn and posterior root with suspected degenerative tearing at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. No meniscal extrusion or displaced fragment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss/fraying about the central weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal partial thickness chondrosis central femoral trochlea. Patellar cartilage is intact. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Bowing of the medial meniscus secondary to adjacent medial meniscal pathology. Otherwise intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain characterized by periligamentous edema.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific subcutaneous soft tissue edema about the anterior knee. Mild deep infrapatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral medial femoral condyle.
2.	Complex tearing of the anterior horn to posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis and osteoarthritis, severe involving the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4.	Grade 1 sprain LCL.
5.	Moderate complex Baker's cyst containing multiple calcified bodies.

Report:
Clinical information: 7 days post soccer injury with valgus shift. Medial collateral ligament testing positive. Medial collateral ligament tear? Partial posterior cruciate ligament tear?

Technique: Unenhanced point tender multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
The medial and lateral meniscus are intact.

There is a slightly increased T2 signal within the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament as a construct is intact. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. The collateral ligaments are intact.

The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a focal avulsed, unhealed bone fragment at the inferior patellar pole. There is no focal bone marrow edema.

There is a focal area of extensive subchondral bone marrow edema in the weightbearing portion of the lateral tibial plateau with associated, nondisplaced subchondral fracture (17-9). There is a focal area of subcortical bone marrow edema at the anterolateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and at the anteromedial aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

There is a minimal superficial chondrosis in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with focal superficial cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet measuring 0.4 cm from medial to lateral.

There is mild joint effusion. There is a low volume Baker's cyst. The Infrapatellar fat pad is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Nondisplaced, subchondral fracture of the lateral tibial plateau with associated bone marrow edema. Posttraumatic contusions at the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral femoral condyles.
2. Low-grade partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No acute injury of the medial collateral ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.
3. Previous unhealed avulsion fracture at the inferior patellar pole.
4. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with a focal area of cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet.

Il y a un émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle. Il y a également une extrusion relativement significative du corps méniscal, le plus probablement en lien avec une déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne. 

Il y a une déchirure complète du ligament colléral interne distal avec rétraction proximale des fibres déchirées, associées à de multiples zones d'irrégularités, épaississements et signal anormal intra-substance. Il y également une atténuation et signal intra-substance à son origine. La partie distale du ligament collatéral interne déchirée se situe légèrement sous les tendons de la patte d'oie constituant une lésion de type ''pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchire complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et une déchirure partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale. 

Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale interne.

Le ménisque externe est intact sans déchirure. Il y a une petite fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné potentiellement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Minime déplacement et œdème associés. L'insertion distale du ligament collatéral externe et du tendon du biceps est préservé de même que l'origine. Il y a également une petite ossification au versant postérieur de la tête du péroné mesurant 5 mm, d'origine indéterminée. 

Il y a des irrégularités de l'os sous-chondral à la surface portante du condyle fémoral externe d'allure plutôt chronique. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale externe. Toutefois, petit foyer d'œdème au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe avec léger hypersignal chondral, contusion versus lésion oséto-chondrale (atypique) versus changement de stress en lien avec l’origine du gastrocnémien externe. 

Kyste ganglionnaire à l'origine des deux gastrocnémiens.

Il y a une déchirure d'allure complète à l'insertion distale du ligament croisé postérieur et/ou avulsion du LCP. Le ligament est rétracté proximalement, épaissi et de signal anormal. Il y a une atténuation significative du ligament croisé antérieur sans composante transfixiante toutefois notée, en lien avec une déchirure partielle. Il y a des contusions probablement associées au plateau tibial externe, plus marquées en postérieur +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale.

Petit kyste ganglionnaire à l'empreinte distale du ligament croisé antérieur.

L'alignement patello-fémoral demeure dans les limites normales. Séquelles de maladie Osgood Schlatter avec fragmentation d'allure chronique de la tubérosité tibiale et léger épaississement du tendon rotulien. Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact sans déchirure. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante patello-fémorale. La graisse de Hoffa est sans grande particularité.

Il y a un œdème diffus significatif sous-cutané et inter-musculaire. Il y a également un œdème des muscles poplité et plantaire en lien avec une entorse.

Conclusion:

Déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne distal avec déplacement de la portion distale sous les tendons de la patte d'oie en lien avec une lésion de type 'pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchirure complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale.

Déchirure d'allure complète du ligament croisé postérieur distal et/ou avulsion du LCP. Déchirure partielle probable du ligament croisé antérieur.

Fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné probablement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Œdème associé.

De plus, contusions probable du plateau tibial externe +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale et du versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe. 

Émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle.

Épanchement intra-articulaire modéré avec composante de lipohémarthrose suspectée.

Dans ce contexte, un complément d'investigation par tomodensitométrie est recommandé pour mieux évaluer les structures osseuses. De plus, une consultation en chirurgie orthopédique est également, fortement recommandée.

report-english-translation:
The following findings:
Moderate intra-articular discharge, with suspicion of a level of fat on the outer side suggesting a degree of lipohaemarthrosis. No significant Baker's cyst with a fluid lyser within the hollow poplite and upper portion of the goose leg.
There is a blistering of the posterior edge of the posterior horn of the internal meniscus suspecting a potential peripheral longitudinal vertical tear. There is also a relatively significant extrusion of the meniscal body, most likely related to a complete tear of the internal collateral ligament.
There is a complete tear of the distal inner collar ligament with proximal retraction of the torn fibers, associated with multiple areas of irregularities, thickening and abnormal intra-substance signal. There is also an intra-substance mitigation and signal at its origin. The distal part of the torn inner collateral ligament is slightly below the tendons of the goose leg, forming a 'pseudo Stener' type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep menisco-femoral component and a partial tear in the menisco-tibial component.
No damage to the internal femoral transverse chondral.
The external meniscus is intact without tearing. There is a small fracture on the upper slope of the head of the peroneum potentially at the insertion of the arched poplite ligament. Minimum movement and associated edema. The distal insertion of the external collateral ligament and biceps tendon is preserved as is the original. There is also a small ossification on the posterior slope of the head of the peroneum measuring 5 mm, of undetermined origin.
There are irregularities in the subchondral bone on the carrier surface of the rather chronic-looking external femoral condyle. No damage to the external femoral transverse chondral. However, small oedema on the posterior side of the external femoral condyle with slight chondral hypersignal, contusion versus osteo-chondral (atypical) injury versus change in stress related to the origin of external gastrocnemia.
The ganglion cyst at the origin of the two gastrocnemians.
There is a full-scale tear at the distal insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament and/or avulsion of the LCP. The ligament is nearly retracted, thick, and has an abnormal signal. There is a significant attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament with no transfixing component however noted, due to partial tear. There are probably contusions associated with the external tibial plateau, more marked in the posterior +/- impaction/subchondral fracture.
A small ganglion cyst with the distal fingerprint of the anterior cruciate ligament.
The patello-femoral alignment remains within normal limits. Sequels of Osgood Schlatter's disease with chronic-looking fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity and slight thickening of the rotulian tendon. The tendon of the distal quadriceps is intact without tearing. No damage to the femoral-patello transfixing chondral. Hoffa's fat is nothing special.
There's significant diffuse subcutaneous and intermuscular edema. There is also edema of the popliteal and plantar muscles associated with a sprain.
Conclusion:
Complete tear of the distal inner collateral ligament with displacement of the distall portion under the tendons of the goose leg in connection with a 'pseudo Stener' type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep menis-femoral component and a partial tear in the menis-tibial component.
Complete tear of the distal posterior cruciate ligament and/or avulsion of the LCP. Possible partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Fracture at the upper slope of the head of the peroneum probably at the insertion of the arched popliteal ligament. Associated edema.
In addition, probable contusions of the external tibial plateau +/- subchondral impaction/fracture and the posterior side of the external femoral condyle.
Removal of the posterior edge of the posterior horn of the internal meniscus suspected of a potential peripheral longitudinal vertical tear.
Moderate intra-articular leakage with suspected lipohaemarthrosis component.
In this context, a complementary CT scan is recommended to better assess bone structures. In addition, consultation with orthopedic surgeons is also highly recommended.

Findings:
There is a radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 4.5 x 3.5 mm. There is an fraying of the residual posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There are no displaced meniscal fragments. There is a moderate mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no acute tear of the lateral meniscus.

The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is a moderate thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial and lateral femorotibial joint compartment. 

There is an mild chondrosis at the medial and lateral patellar facet with focal superficial cartilage irregularities at the lateral patellar facet. There are no cartilage defects, no subchondral bone marrow edema.

There is no joint effusion. There is no Baker's cyst. 

The joint articulations are well-maintained. 

There is a lobulated ganglion cyst extending along the popliteus tendon measuring 4.5 x 1.4 cm in the axial plane.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. The visualized muscle bulk is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No displaced meniscal fragments. 
2. No acute ligamentous injury, especially no tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
3. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

Oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the medial meniscus involving body and posterior horn with associated para meniscal cyst posteriorly.

Interprétation : 

Il y a un minime liséré de liquide au récessus suprapatellaire externe, inchangé, le plus probablement en lien avec une accumulation physiologique. Il n'y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Il y a un petit kyste de Baker allongé, inchangé, s’étendant sur environ 4 cm de diamètre crâniocaudal. Il n'y a pas de signe de complication. 

Le ménisque interne est inchangé, sans déchirure notée. Il y a de légers changements dégénératifs au compartiment fémorotibial interne avec fissures chondrales superficielles, une atténuation chondrale, en particulier à la surface portante, et de petits ostéophytes marginaux. Il y a un nouveau petit foyer d’œdème non-spécifique au plateau tibial postéro-interne, au versant plus central, non-spécifique. Il n'y a pas de trait fracturaire ni d’impaction trabéculaire noté. Il pourrait s’agir d’une petite contusion osseuse ou des changements réactionnels en lien avec l’insertion distale du ligament croisé postérieur à proximité. 

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact et sans déchirure.

Le ménisque externe est inchangé, sans déchirure notée. Il y a de minimes changements dégénératifs au compartiment fémorotibial externe avec une légère atténuation chondrale et des ébauches ostéophytiques aux marges articulaires. 

Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact et sans déchirure.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure. À nouveau, il y a un petit kyste intra-osseux ganglionnaire sous l’insertion au niveau des épines tibiales. 

Il y a des nouveaux foyers de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels aux deux versants de l’articulation tibiofibulaire proximal, le plus probablement de nature dégénérative. 

Il y a, à nouveau, une bascule/subluxation externe de la rotule de même que de larges enthésophytes/ossifications à l’origine du tendon patellaire. Il y a une légère progression d’un épaississement marqué diffus du tendon patellaire, en particulier au tiers proximal, compatible avec une tendinose sévère sous-jacente. Dans l’intervalle, il y a une nouvelle déchirure partielle, intra-substance focale proximale à l’origine du tendon patellaire sous le pôle inférieur de la rotule, avec un léger déplacement caudal d’une ossification, potentiellement de nature avulsive. Celle-ci parait de grade intermédiaire à important, impliquant plus de 50% de l’épaisseur tendineuse à l’origine du tendon, dont la composante principale mesure environ 11 x 12 x 10 mm. 

La déchirure intrasubstance partielle précédemment décrite à l’insertion distale impliquant les fibres profondes du tendon patellaire parait résolue avec principalement une tendinose résiduelle distalement. 

Il y a un léger œdème réactionnel au pôle inférieur de la rotule. Il y a aussi une infiltration associée de la graisse de Hoffa. 

Il y a un minime épaississement prépatellaire et infrapatellaire résiduel, sans franche composante de bursite à l’étude actuelle. 

Par ailleurs, il y a de légers changements dégénératifs au compartiment patellofémoral avec fissures chondrales superficielles. Ceci est plus marqué à l’apex patellaire et à la facette patellaire externe avec de petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

La rotule est légèrement hautement située avec un minime œdème également au sein de la graisse de Hoffa supéro-externe pour laquelle un syndrome de friction entre le tendon patellaire et le condyle fémoral externe est suggéré tel que précédemment mentionné.

Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact et sans déchirure. 

Conclusion :

Il y a légère progression d’une tendinose déjà sévère impliquant le tendon patellaire, particulièrement à son tiers proximal, telle que décrite ci-haut, avec principalement une nouvelle déchirure partielle focale potentiellement de type avulsive et de grade intermédiaire à important à son origine sous le pôle inférieur de la rotule telle que décrite ci-haut. Il y a un léger œdème réactionnel au pôle inférieur de la rotule. 

Il y a résolution dans l'intervalle d’une déchirure précédemment décrite distalement au sein du tendon patellaire.

Il y a de nouveaux foyers de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels à l’articulation tibiofibulaire proximale, probablement de nature dégénérative de même qu’une petite contusion osseuse versus changements réactionnels au versant postérieur légèrement central du plateau tibial interne tels que détaillés ci-haut. 

Il n'y a pas d’autre changement significatif dans l’intervalle.

Report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right-sided knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, consistent with extensive complex tearing. The anterior horn shows intrasubstance degeneration without tear. The posterior root is barely perceptible consistent with extensive complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body.

Barely perceptible posterior root of the lateral meniscus raising suspicion for complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. No lateral meniscal extrusion. 

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with intrasubstance ganglion formation. Slight anterior tibial translation.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament near the medial femoral condyle origin. The meniscotibial meniscal femoral component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact. The posterior oblique ligament is intact.

Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis of the lateral femoral condylar attachment, without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 15 mm, at the upper limit of normal. No patellofemoral subluxation.

There is focal full thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex with fissuring of articular cartilage at the patellar apex and extending along the medial patellar facet. There is diffuse full-thickness cartilage denuding throughout the weightbearing aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment with subchondral sclerosis. There is mild to moderate lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Prominent non-marginal lateral femoral condylar osteophyte.

Trace knee joint fluid. Subcutaneous edema along the lateral and posterior aspects of the knee and proximal calf. There is generalized atrophy of the regional musculature which maybe on the basis of deconditioning. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Extensive complex tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and tricompartment chondrosis as pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Suspected complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Borderline lateralization of the tibial tubercle which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
6. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with slight anterior tibial translation.

.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

Buckling of the posterior cruciate ligament is noted in association with the anterior tibial drawer. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament is intact. There is some mild intrinsic signal around the deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament in keeping with a low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact including the fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, the popliteus tendon and the IT band.

There is an undisplaced vertical tear of the peripheral one third of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the posterior aspect of the posterior body. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment are well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is no significant Baker's cyst or significant knee effusion. There is mild reactive synovitis within the joint.

INTERPRETATION: 

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear of mid fibers associated with a significant anterior tibial drawer.

Resolving kissing bone contusions in association with pivot shift mechanism of injury.

Low-grade sprain of the medial fibers of medial collateral ligament.

Undisplaced radial tear of peripheral one third of posterior horn of medial meniscus extending into posterior body.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain for 3 months.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the body and posterior horn extending into the posterior root with a predominant vertical longitudinal component. Minimal peripheral extrusion of the body segment.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects. Incidental dorsal defect of the patella in the superolateral quadrant.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate distal quadriceps tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing of the lateral insertional fibers and some underlying edema within the suprapatellar fat.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 3 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tearing of the medial meniscal body/posterior horn.
2. Moderate distal quadriceps tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing of the lateral insertional fibers.

Conclusion: No significant abnormality identified.

.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

Low proton density/low T2 signal lesion within the anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle measuring 23 x 9 x 9 mm without aggressive imaging features, likely representing a bone island.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits.

2. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
3. Probable bone island medial femoral condyle; plain film correlation recommended for confirmation.
4. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

Report:
Interprétation:

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire avec signes de synovite chronique. Il y a un également un kyste de Baker associé à une prolifération synoviale/synovite chronique s'étendant sur environ 5 cm de diamètre cc. Celui-ci s'étend au niveau des bourses du semi-membraneux et de la patte d'oie avec composante de bursite probablement associée. 

Il y a une déchirure complexe du ménisque interne avec déchirure radiaire transfixiante à la jonction de la racine postérieure et de la corne postérieure, et déchirure longitudinale horizontale impliquant la corne postérieure résiduelle, corps méniscal et s'étendant à la jonction avec la corne antérieure. Il y a une extrusion marquée du corps méniscal de façon associée. De plus, il y a une structure légèrement hétérogène et principalement hypointense ovalaire située de façon intime avec le rebord postérieur de la racine postérieure du ménisque interne mesurant 7 x 14 x 7 mm. L'aspect est plutôt en faveur d'une souris intra-articulaire qui pourrait être en partie ossifiée versus un ossicule méniscal (moins probable). L'aspect est moins en faveur d'un ''flap'' méniscal dont le signal demeure légèrement différent du ménisque et sans continuité démontrée avec la corne postérieure. 

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne avec atteinte transfixiante aux surfaces portantes et petits ostéophytes marginaux. Pas de changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé. 

Le ménisque externe de même que le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts sans déchirure. 

Légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe, plus marquée à la surface portante. Petits ostéophytes marginaux.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Petit kyste ganglionnaire para-ligamentaire.

L'alignement patello-fémoral est préservé. Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact sans déchirure. Légère tendinose du patellaire sans déchirure. 

Atténuation modérée des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patello-fémoral avec fissure chondrale partielle le long de la surface articulaire patellaire et atteinte transfixiante le long de la surface trochléaire. Pas de changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé. Petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Conclusion:

Déchirure complexe du ménisque interne avec composante radiaire transfixiante à la jonction de la corne postérieure et de la racine postérieure avec extrusion significative du corps méniscal secondairement, de plus, déchirure longitudinale horizontale de la corne postérieure résiduelle et du corps du ménisque interne s'étendant à la jonction avec la corne antérieure.

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie tricompartimentaux de grade 3 impliquant les compartiments fémoro-tibiaux interne et patello-fémoral et de grade 1 impliquant le compartiment fémoro-tibial externe.

Petit épanchement intra-articulaire et kyste de Baker avec signes de synovite chronique associée. Bursite du semi-membraneux et de la patte d'oie avec également synovite d'allure chronique associée. 

Souris intra-articulaire potentiellement en partie ossifiée au rebord postérieur de la racine postérieure du ménisque interne. Un ossicule méniscal paraît moins probable. L'aspect est moins en faveur d'un ''flap'' méniscal avec un signal différent du ménisque et sans continuité notée avec la corne postérieure du ménisque interne.
